recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should only revisit the wording if FHIR-I decides to change the conformance obligation for profile assertions after order-changing transformations.
issue_request: FHIR-12331 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core change request from DSTU2 asking for explicit guidance that clients should not depend on servers maintaining element order unless a profile mandates it, and that servers unable to preserve such order must remove profile assertions that may depend on ordering.
initial_application: The Jira comments identify svn revision 11203. Git commit 8c3813303ed3c8d0e5efe695af4639ec6a9ecf9a, imported from that revision, added the repeating-element ordering note to source/conformance-rules.html alongside the cardinality/orderMeaning discussion. The same commit also handled FHIR-12311 by adding ElementDefinition.orderMeaning context.
additional_context: The current build still includes conformance-rules.html through source/hierarchy.xml. The current conformance text states that repeating-element order may have meaning, links to ElementDefinition.orderMeaning, says implementations may reorder when no order meaning is defined, and carries the FHIR-12331 warning about profile tags. The resource metadata/profile-tag guidance separately explains that profile tags are discovery assertions, not meaning, and that servers may update or remove tags when an update invalidates them. The original Zulip thread supports the current scope, and no Confluence references or later core Jira results were found that require a different current-source change.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the requested warning is already present in an active conformance page and adding duplicate prose to the profiling page would not change implementer obligations.

related_jiras.note: Implemented in the same svn revision by adding ElementDefinition.orderMeaning, which is the mechanism referenced by the current FHIR-12331 conformance prose. It was not independently decided in this seed run.
Related Jira search found this applied EU Laboratory IG issue using similar ordering terms, but it is outside FHIR-core and does not affect the seed decision.
